title: Polynomials in f Commute
content: commute_of_mem_adjoin_singleton shows any two elements of the subalgebra K[f] = adjoin K {f} commute: each is some aeval f p, aeval f q, and these commute because polynomial evaluation is an algebra map (map_mul) and K[X] is commutative (mul_comm). This single fact silently supplies the commutation clause [s, n] = 0 of the whole decomposition — once both parts are produced inside K[f], their commuting is automatic, never separately argued.
mathContext: $$a = p(f),\ b = q(f) \;\Rightarrow\; ab = (pq)(f) = (qp)(f) = ba.$$ The subalgebra $K[f]$ is commutative.

title: Each Part Commutes with f
content: commute_part_self specializes the previous lemma to the generator: since f itself lies in adjoin K {f} (self_mem_adjoin_singleton), any element a of K[f] commutes with f. So the semisimple and nilpotent parts — being polynomials in f — commute with f as well as with each other, the structural backbone of the decomposition.

title: Existence: f = s + n, Both Polynomials in f
content: jordan_chevalley_decomposition establishes existence over a finite-dimensional space and a PERFECT field: f = s + n with s semisimple, n nilpotent, [s,n] = 0, and explicit witnesses s = aeval f p, n = aeval f q. It wraps Mathlib's Module.End.exists_isNilpotent_isSemisimple, whose Newton-iteration proof (after Chambert-Loir) constructs both parts inside adjoin K {f}; membership there is what yields the polynomial witnesses (Algebra.adjoin_mem_exists_aeval) and the commutation for free. The perfect-field hypothesis is essential — over a non-perfect field the semisimple part may fail to be a polynomial in f.
mathContext: $$f = s + n, \quad s \text{ semisimple},\ n \text{ nilpotent},\ [s,n]=0, \quad s = p(f),\ n = q(f).$$

title: Uniqueness via 'Semisimple ∧ Nilpotent ⟹ 0'
content: jordan_chevalley_unique proves two polynomial-in-f decompositions coincide. From s₁ + n₁ = s₂ + n₂ rearrange to s₁ − s₂ = n₂ − n₁. The left side is a difference of commuting semisimple operators, hence semisimple over a perfect field (IsSemisimple.sub_of_commute) — the key new Mathlib ingredient; the right side is a difference of commuting nilpotents, hence nilpotent. Being both semisimple and nilpotent forces it to be zero (eq_zero_of_isNilpotent_isSemisimple), so s₁ = s₂ and then n₁ = n₂ by cancellation. The commutation needed throughout comes for free from all four parts living in K[f].
mathContext: $$s_1 - s_2 = n_2 - n_1 \text{ is both semisimple and nilpotent} \Rightarrow s_1 - s_2 = 0 \Rightarrow s_1=s_2,\ n_1=n_2.$$
prerequisites: difference of commuting semisimples is semisimple
difference of commuting nilpotents is nilpotent

title: Packaged ExistsUnique
content: jordan_chevalley_existsUnique combines existence and uniqueness into a single ExistsUnique statement: there is a unique pair (s, n), both in adjoin K {f}, with s semisimple, n nilpotent, and f = s + n. Existence reuses exists_isNilpotent_isSemisimple; uniqueness applies jordan_chevalley_unique to any competing pair, then Prod.ext_iff packages the two component equalities. Mathlib supplies the existence and the sub_of_commute lemma but, per the file header, still lists this packaged ExistsUnique form as a TODO — so the entry fills a genuine library gap.
mathContext: $$\exists!\,(s,n) \in K[f]^2:\ s \text{ semisimple} \wedge n \text{ nilpotent} \wedge f = s+n.$$
